hormuz_disruption.label: Iran / Hormuz Disruption
hormuz_disruption.last_note: Ceasefire is extended indefinitely but the strait remains commercially near-dead at roughly 5% of pre-conflict vessel traffic, and Iran reimposed restrictions after Lebanon violations, keeping the disruption very real but a deal framework could materialize within days per Trump.

stagflation_regime.label: Stagflation Regime
stagflation_regime.last_note: May CPI is set to print 4.2% today, core PCE nowcast sits at 4.18%, PPI already surged 6% in April, real wages are negative, and CME FedWatch now prices a 40% chance of a rate hike by December with zero cuts in 2026 — the stagflation regime is fully in force.

ai_bubble_risk.label: AI Bubble Risk Q4 2026
ai_bubble_risk.last_note: The Fed has formally listed AI as a top systemic risk, hyperscaler capex is confirmed at $725B for 2026 with capital intensity at 45-57% of revenue, yet cloud backlogs remain full and AI capacity is being absorbed as fast as it is deployed, keeping the bubble risk elevated but not yet breaking.

gold_supercycle.label: Gold Supercycle
gold_supercycle.last_note: Gold has corrected from a $5,405 peak to $4,183 today on ceasefire signals and higher-for-longer rate expectations, but JPMorgan targets $5,000 by Q4 2026 and structural central bank demand of 755 tonnes per year keeps the supercycle thesis alive through the correction.

copper_deficit.label: Structural Copper Deficit
copper_deficit.last_note: Copper fell roughly 6% over the prior three sessions on hawkish Fed repricing and dollar strength, global visible inventory has risen by 540,000 metric tons year-to-date, and JPMorgan warns bearish macro risks dominate near-term price action even though the structural deficit remains intact post-2029.

nuclear_renaissance.label: Nuclear Renaissance
nuclear_renaissance.last_note: Oklo closed the ARMEC precision-manufacturing acquisition on June 4 to tighten its deployment timeline, Vistra and other nuclear names remain in active hyperscaler power-purchase deals, and global data center electricity demand is on track to double by 2026 per the IEA, cementing the structural demand case.

ALAB.note: Astera Labs posted record Q1 2026 revenue of $308.4M with guidance exceeding $800M for fiscal 2026, confirming the AI connectivity thesis is intact operationally, but the P/E of 81 leaves extreme multiple-compression risk if the AI capex cycle decelerates in H2 2026.

POWL.note: The data center electrical equipment thesis is structurally valid given the confirmed $725B AI capex wave, but P/E of 41 and slowing backlog visibility in a rising-rate stagflation regime limit near-term upside, and no new catalyst has emerged today.

MOD.note: Negative FCF of -$101M is a direct red flag in a high-rate stagflation environment where capital is expensive, and while the thermal management thesis for data centers is structurally sound, MOD is drifting from a growth story toward a balance-sheet-risk story.

GFS.note: The CHIPS Act thesis remains a show-me story with no new catalysts today, and GFS continues to trade on optionality rather than earnings momentum, making it vulnerable to further multiple compression if the macro stays hawkish.

CRDO.note: Credo is riding the same AI connectivity wave as ALAB with strong revenue momentum, but the lack of FCF and high valuation mean it has drifted from a growth-at-reasonable-price thesis toward a pure-momentum trade vulnerable to any AI capex sentiment shift.

ARM.note: ARM at P/E 105 and only $750M FCF is priced for perfection in a stagflation regime where the Fed may hike; the royalty model thesis is structurally brilliant but the entry price has not corrected enough relative to the macro risk, making it a valuation trap today.

S.note: SentinelOne posted non-GAAP diluted EPS of $0.04 in Q1 FY2027 versus a loss of $0.63 a year ago, showing genuine margin progress, but at $15.24 and still carrying a large accumulated deficit of $2.15B, the turnaround thesis is early-stage and fragile in a risk-off macro environment.

ZS.note: Zscaler increased annual recurring revenue 26% year-over-year to over $3 billion with 52% free cash flow margin and has only 45% penetration of Fortune 500 companies suggesting significant runway, but the stock is 62.7% below its 52-week high and the negative EV/EBITDA reflects that the market has repriced the zero-trust premium — the business thesis is partially intact but the original growth premium valuation thesis is broken.

AXON.note: AXON at EV/EBITDA of 379 and only $63M FCF is a thesis that has fully drifted — the original public-safety AI growth story is intact operationally but the valuation at 48.9% below its 52-week high is still not cheap enough to justify re-entry given negative real rates and stagflation headwinds on discretionary government spending.

ISRG.note: Intuitive Surgical has zero debt, $4.5B cash, 23% revenue growth, and $2.3B FCF making it a genuine compounder, but at 36x forward earnings and 29.4% below highs the surgical robotics moat thesis is unchanged — the drift is purely valuation-related, not fundamental, and the stock remains a hold-not-add until the multiple contracts further.

RXRX.note: Recursion Pharmaceuticals has revenue growth of minus 56.1%, is burning $178M in FCF with negative operating margins of minus 1985%, and is 55.2% below its 52-week high — the original AI drug discovery thesis has collapsed as clinical pipeline progress has not justified the technology premium and this is now a capital destruction story with no near-term catalyst.

JEDI.note: The drone and modern warfare rearmament thesis is structurally intact given the Hormuz crisis has accelerated defense technology procurement, but at 25% below highs and with no fundamental data available for an ETF wrapper this remains a theme trade that requires a defined technical base before adding risk.

CWAN.note: Clearwater Analytics has 74.4% revenue growth and $160M FCF which is operationally compelling, but analyst targets of $24.47 to $24.55 against the current $24.35 price provide virtually zero upside consensus — at PEG of 10.24 and EV/EBITDA of 73.69 the institutional fintech thesis is fully priced with no margin of safety.

GRAB.note: Grab at $3.30 with $6.5B cash, 23.5% revenue growth, and PEG of 0.87 is the most asymmetric deep value setup in the portfolio on a pure fundamentals basis, but the stock is 50.2% below highs and the Southeast Asia super-app monetization thesis requires a specific catalyst such as a buyback announcement or profitability upgrade to unlock value — thesis intact, no trigger yet.
